distractors.misconception: leaving the bare verb although 'have' needs the past participle after it
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “has” kata kerjanya harus past participle “flown”, bukan “fly” polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dibiarin polos padahal sesudah have butuh past participle.

distractors.misconception: mixes 'have' with a finite past form of 'be' instead of the participle
distractors.whyFailsId: “has” berpasangan sama past participle, bukan -ing. “Never” juga tempatnya sesudah “has”.
distractors.misconceptionId: have dicampur sama bentuk -ing, bukan past participle.

explain.why: Rentang waktunya seumur hidup sampai sekarang, dan “she always travels by train” nunjukin itu masih berlaku, jadi “has never flown” yang pas.
explain.rule: Pengalaman hidup tanpa waktu pasti: have/has + never/ever + past participle.
explain.memory: Belum pernah seumur hidup → has never flown.
explain.avoid: Nggak ada tanggal atau kata waktu selesai? Pakai have/has + past participle.

items.sentence: Mr. Hadi has taught at our school ___ ten years, and he still loves it.

distractors.misconception: uses 'since' before a length of time
distractors.whyFailsId: “since” buat titik mulai kayak 2015, bukan lamanya kayak “ten years”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “since” di depan lamanya waktu, padahal since buat titik mulai.

distractors.misconception: sealing the period off as a completed event, though the family still lives there
distractors.whyFailsId: “during” bilang kapan sesuatu terjadi di dalam suatu masa, bukan ngukur berapa lama keadaan itu bertahan.
distractors.misconceptionId: rentangnya ditutup seolah udah selesai.

distractors.misconception: uses 'for' before a starting point
distractors.whyFailsId: “from” butuh titik akhir (“from 2015 to 2025”). Sendirian, dia nggak bisa ngikut present perfect di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “for” di depan titik mulai, padahal for buat lamanya waktu.

explain.why: “Ten years” itu lamanya waktu, jadi present perfect-nya pakai “for”: has taught for ten years.
explain.rule: Present perfect + for + lamanya waktu. Present perfect + since + titik mulai.
explain.memory: Lamanya waktu pakai “for”, titik mulai pakai “since”: “for ten years”, “since 2015”.
explain.avoid: Tanya: ini jumlah tahun atau tanggal? Jumlah → for. Tanggal → since.

items.sentence: The traffic today is ___ than yesterday. We will be late.

distractors.misconception: regular -er ending forced onto an irregular adjective
distractors.whyFailsId: “bad” itu tak beraturan, nggak pernah pakai -er.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran -er dipaksain ke kata sifat tak beraturan.

distractors.misconception: regular 'more + adjective' pattern applied to an irregular adjective
distractors.whyFailsId: “more bad” ngikutin pola biasa, padahal “bad” punya bentuk sendiri: worse.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola “more + kata sifat” dipakai buat kata sifat tak beraturan.

distractors.misconception: superlative 'best' used where 'than' demands a comparative
distractors.whyFailsId: “worst” buat bandingin tiga atau lebih. “Than” nandain perbandingan dua hal.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk paling dipakai padahal “than” minta bentuk banding.

explain.why: “Than” minta bentuk banding, dan bentuk banding “bad” itu “worse”.
explain.rule: Bentuk banding tak beraturan: good → better, bad → worse, far → further.
explain.memory: Hafalin pasangannya: good jadi better, bad jadi worse.
explain.avoid: Hafalin daftar pendek pasangan tak beraturan sebelum kamu ambil -er atau more.

items.sentence: This book is ___ (interesting) than the film.

distractors.misconception: adds -er to a long adjective
distractors.whyFailsId: “interesting” tiga suku kata, jadi pakai “more”, bukan -er.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin -er ke kata sifat panjang, padahal yang panjang pakai more.

distractors.misconception: doubles the comparative marking by putting 'more' before an adjective already ending in '-er'
distractors.whyFailsId: “more” dan -er sama-sama nandain banding. Pakai satu aja.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda bandingnya dobel: more plus -er.

distractors.misconception: uses the superlative after 'the' for a two-item comparison
distractors.whyFailsId: “than” bandingin dua hal, jadi butuh bentuk banding, bukan bentuk paling.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai bentuk paling, padahal cuma dua hal yang dibandingin.

explain.why: “Interesting” kata sifat panjang, jadi bentuk bandingnya “more interesting”.
explain.rule: Kata sifat pendek pakai -er (cheaper). Kata sifat panjang pakai more (more interesting). Jangan dua-duanya.
explain.memory: Kata panjang → more. Kata pendek → -er.
explain.avoid: Ucapin kata sifatnya: tiga suku kata atau lebih → more.

items.sentence: Be careful, the soup is very ___.

distractors.misconception: uses the adverb where an adjective after 'be' is needed
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “is”, katanya ngegambarin supnya sendiri, jadi harus kata sifat, bukan -ly.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai bentuk -ly sesudah is/are, padahal sesudah be yang dibutuhin kata sifat.

distractors.misconception: uses the bare adjective after an action verb where a manner adverb in '-ly' is required
distractors.whyFailsId: “heat” itu kata benda atau kata kerja. “Very” butuh kata sifat sesudahnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata benda dipakai di tempat kata sifat.

distractors.misconception: switches to a comparative adjective although nothing is being compared and the slot needs an adverb
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada yang dibandingin, dan “very” nggak cocok sama bentuk banding.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk banding dipakai padahal nggak ada yang dibandingin.

explain.why: “Is” nyambungin sup sama gambarannya, jadi butuh kata sifat “hot”.
explain.rule: Sesudah be (am/is/are) pakai kata sifat. Sesudah kata kerja aksi pakai kata keterangan -ly.
explain.memory: Sesudah is pakai kata sifat: is hot. Sesudah kata kerja aksi pakai -ly: walks slowly.
explain.avoid: Ada is/are di depan titik-titik? Pilih kata sifat polos.

items.sentence: ___ brothers and sisters do you have?

distractors.misconception: asks about a countable plural noun with 'how much'
distractors.whyFailsId: “brothers and sisters” bisa dihitung, jadi kata tanyanya “how many”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nanya benda yang bisa dihitung pakai “how much”, padahal harusnya “how many”.

distractors.misconception: asks quantity with bare 'how' and drops the quantity word entirely
distractors.whyFailsId: “how” sendirian nanya cara, bukan jumlah.
distractors.misconceptionId: nanya jumlah cuma pakai “how”, kata jumlahnya hilang.

distractors.misconception: adds a partitive 'of' straight after 'how much' before a bare noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “of” cuma pas di depan “the/your/them”: how many of your friends, bukan how many of brothers.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin “of” langsung di depan kata benda polos.

explain.why: “Brothers and sisters” bisa dihitung dan jamak, jadi pertanyaannya mulai dari “How many”.
explain.rule: How many + kata benda jamak yang bisa dihitung. How much + kata benda yang nggak bisa dihitung.
explain.memory: Bisa dihitung → how many.
explain.avoid: Bisa ditaruh angka di depannya (two brothers)? Tanyanya pakai “How many”.

items.sentence: Sorry, I ___ the answer right now.

distractors.misconception: Assumes present time always requires present continuous.
distractors.whyFailsId: “know” kata kerja keadaan, jadi tetap present simple walau ada “right now”.
distractors.misconceptionId: ngira waktu sekarang selalu butuh bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: reduces the sentence to a fragment: an -ing form with no finite verb to carry the tense
distractors.whyFailsId: negatif present simple butuh “don't”. “Not know” polos bukan kata kerja utuh.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya jadi potongan tanpa kata kerja utuh.

distractors.misconception: bare-verb-without-auxiliary
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “don't” kata kerjanya polos: don't know, bukan don't knowing.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja polos tanpa kata bantu.

explain.why: “Know” ngegambarin keadaan, bukan aksi, jadi walau ada “right now” tetap present simple: don't know.
explain.rule: Kata kerja keadaan (know, like, want, belong) biasanya tetap present simple, bukan bentuk -ing.
explain.memory: Know, like, want: tanpa -ing.
explain.avoid: “Right now” nggak otomatis berarti -ing. Cek dulu kata kerjanya keadaan atau bukan.

items.sentence: We don't have ___ milk left, so I'll buy some.

distractors.misconception: uses 'no' before a verb already negated with 'not'
distractors.whyFailsId: “don't” udah negatif. Nambah “no” bikin negatif dobel.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “no” sesudah kata kerja yang udah negatif, jadi negatifnya dobel.

distractors.misconception: combining a negated verb ('didn't') with a negative pronoun, creating a non-standard double negative
distractors.whyFailsId: “nothing” itu kata ganti negatif, nggak bisa berdiri di depan kata benda “milk” sesudah “don't”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja negatif digabung sama kata ganti negatif.

distractors.misconception: incorrectly splitting the compound negative pronoun into two words
distractors.whyFailsId: “none” ngegantiin kata benda (“we have none”), nggak bisa langsung di depan “milk”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti dipakai di depan kata benda.

explain.why: “Don't have” udah negatif, jadi kata bendanya pakai “any”: don't have any milk.
explain.rule: Satu negatif per klausa: don't + any, atau have + no. Jangan don't + no.
explain.memory: Satu negatif aja: don't … any, atau have … no.
explain.avoid: Hitung negatifnya. Kalau kata kerjanya udah ada “not”, kata berikutnya “any”.

items.sentence: If I had more free time, I ___ a new language.

distractors.misconception: real/likely framing applied to an admittedly unlikely event
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” buat rencana nyata. “Had” yang lampau nunjukin ini khayalan, jadi butuh “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: situasi yang jelas nggak nyata dibingkai seolah nyata.

distractors.misconception: if-clause verb form mismatched with 'would' in the main clause
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple tempatnya di klausa if. Klausa akibat butuh “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk klausa if nyasar ke klausa akibat.

distractors.misconception: duplicating 'would' in both clauses
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “would” kata kerjanya polos: would learn, bukan would learned.
distractors.misconceptionId: would digabung sama bentuk -ed.

explain.why: “If I had more free time” ngegambarin keadaan sekarang yang nggak nyata, jadi akibatnya pakai “would learn”.
explain.rule: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + kata kerja dasar.
explain.memory: Khayalan sekarang: If I had…, I would…
explain.avoid: Ada klausa if bentuk lampau soal khayalan sekarang? Taruh “would” plus kata kerja polos di akibatnya.

items.sentence: Your sister works at the hospital, ___?

distractors.misconception: uses a positive tag after a positive statement
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya positif, jadi tag-nya harus dibalik jadi negatif: doesn't she.
distractors.misconceptionId: tag-nya positif sesudah kalimat positif, padahal harusnya dibalik jadi negatif.

distractors.misconception: wrong auxiliary borrowed from a different tense
distractors.whyFailsId: “works” itu present simple, jadi tag-nya butuh “does”, bukan “is”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantunya nyasar dari bentuk lain.

distractors.misconception: repeats the noun instead of using a pronoun in the tag
distractors.whyFailsId: tag pakai kata ganti, bukan kata benda utuh: doesn't she.
distractors.misconceptionId: ngulang kata bendanya di tag, padahal tag pakai kata ganti.

explain.why: “Works” itu present simple positif, jadi tag-nya negatif pakai “does” dan kata ganti “she”: doesn't she?
explain.rule: Kalimat positif → tag negatif. Tag niru kata bantu kalimatnya dan pakai kata ganti.
explain.memory: Kalimat positif, tag negatif: works → doesn't she?
explain.avoid: Tiga cek: balik positif-negatifnya, samain kata bantunya, ganti kata benda jadi kata ganti.

items.sentence: "What time does the shop open?" → He asked me what time ___.

distractors.misconception: keeps the question-form inversion (auxiliary before subject) inside the reported clause
distractors.whyFailsId: pertanyaan yang dilaporin pakai urutan kalimat berita, jadi “did” nggak boleh di depan “the shop”.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan pertanyaan (kata bantu sebelum subjek) tetap dipakai di klausa laporan.

distractors.misconception: keeps the present tense inside a reported question after a past reporting verb
distractors.whyFailsId: “asked” lampau, jadi “opens” biasanya mundur jadi “opened”.
distractors.misconceptionId: tetap pakai bentuk sekarang di dalam pertanyaan yang dilaporin, padahal kata pelapornya lampau.

distractors.misconception: produces an ungrammatical inversion not used in either direct or reported questions in this pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: ini masih nyimpen urutan pertanyaan sekaligus bentuk sekarang dari pertanyaan langsungnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: inversi yang nggak dipakai di pertanyaan langsung maupun laporan.

explain.why: Di pertanyaan yang dilaporin, subjek duluan baru kata kerja, dan bentuk waktunya mundur: what time the shop opened.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan wh- yang dilaporin: kata tanya + subjek + kata kerja (tanpa do/does/did), bentuk waktunya mundur sesudah kata pelapor lampau.
explain.memory: Asked what time the shop opened: tanpa “did”.
explain.avoid: Buang do/does/did, taruh subjek duluan, lalu geser kata kerjanya satu langkah ke lampau.

items.sentence: Do you know what time ___?

distractors.misconception: keeps direct-question inversion (verb before subject) inside the embedded clause
distractors.whyFailsId: pertanyaannya udah dibikin sama “Do you know”. Bagian dalamnya nggak boleh ngulang bentuk pertanyaan.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan pertanyaan langsung (kata kerja sebelum subjek) tetap dipakai di klausa yang ditempel.

distractors.misconception: adds 'do' to an embedded question
distractors.whyFailsId: urutannya udah bener, tapi “does” nggak dibutuhin. Kata kerjanya cukup pakai -s: closes.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin “do” ke pertanyaan yang ditempel, padahal di dalam kalimat nggak butuh do.

distractors.misconception: moves the auxiliary to the very front of the embedded clause, producing an invalid word order
distractors.whyFailsId: naruh kata kerja sebelum subjek bukan urutan bahasa Inggris di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dipindah ke depan subjek, urutannya nggak sah.

explain.why: Sesudah “Do you know what time”, sisanya kalimat berita biasa: the bank closes.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan nggak langsung: pembuka + kata tanya + subjek + kata kerja. Tanpa do/does/did di bagian dalamnya.
explain.memory: Do you know + kalimat berita.
explain.avoid: Ucapin bagian dalamnya sebagai kalimat berita dulu, baru tempelin.

items.sentence: I can't swim. I wish I ___ swim like my brother.

distractors.misconception: keeping the present tense after 'wish', reading the situation as a real current fact
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “wish” kata kerjanya mundur: “can” jadi “could”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang dibiarin sesudah wish, situasinya dibaca sebagai fakta nyata.

distractors.misconception: uses 'would' in the wish clause about one's own situation
distractors.whyFailsId: “wish + would” buat kelakuan orang lain yang nyebelin, bukan kemampuan diri sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “would” di klausa wish soal diri sendiri, padahal wish + past simple.

distractors.misconception: inserting 'would' for the speaker's own situation, as if the sentence were a result clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” nunjuk masa depan nyata. “Wish” ngegambarin keadaan sekarang yang nggak nyata.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk masa depan nyata dipakai buat harapan yang nggak nyata.

explain.why: Pembicara nggak bisa berenang sekarang dan berharap sebaliknya, jadi “wish” pakai bentuk lampau: could swim.
explain.rule: Wish soal sekarang: wish + past simple (atau could). Can → could.
explain.memory: Nggak bisa sekarang, jadi wish I could: can't swim → wish I could.
explain.avoid: Balik kalimat nyatanya jadi kebalikannya, lalu geser kata kerjanya satu langkah ke lampau.

items.sentence: You don't need to wash the dishes. I ___ them.

distractors.misconception: uses 'yet' in a positive statement
distractors.whyFailsId: “yet” tempatnya di kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan, bukan kalimat positif.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “yet” di kalimat positif, padahal yet buat negatif dan pertanyaan.

distractors.misconception: drags 'just' to the end of the clause instead of mid-position between the auxiliary and the participle
distractors.whyFailsId: “already” duduk di antara “have” dan participle, bukan sebelum “have”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata keterangannya nggak di posisi tengah antara kata bantu dan participle.

distractors.misconception: parks 'still' at the end of a negative clause instead of before the auxiliary
distractors.whyFailsId: “already” dan “yet” nggak bisa digabung. Satu kata udah cukup.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata keterangan waktunya ditumpuk di ujung.

explain.why: Piringnya udah beres, jadi kalimat positifnya pakai “already” di posisi tengah: have already washed.
explain.rule: Have + already/just + past participle di kalimat positif. “Yet” di ujung kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan.
explain.memory: Positif pakai already di tengah, negatif pakai yet di ujung.
explain.avoid: Positif dan udah selesai? Selipin “already” langsung sesudah “have”.

items.sentence: Maya and Dito are best friends. They tell ___ everything.

distractors.misconception: uses a reflexive pronoun where the plain object pronoun is needed
distractors.whyFailsId: “themselves” artinya tiap orang cerita ke dirinya sendiri. Di sini Maya cerita ke Dito dan Dito ke Maya.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai kata ganti diri (-self), padahal pelaku dan objeknya orang yang beda.

distractors.misconception: uses the plain object pronoun although subject and object are the same person
distractors.whyFailsId: “them” nunjuk orang lain di luar mereka berdua, bukan Maya dan Dito.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti objek biasa dipakai padahal subjek dan objeknya orang yang sama.

distractors.misconception: picks a reflexive that does not match the person of the subject
distractors.whyFailsId: “theirselves” bukan kata bahasa Inggris. Bentuknya “themselves”, dan itu pun salah di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti diri yang nggak cocok sama subjeknya.

explain.why: Ceritanya dua arah antara dua orang, jadi “each other” yang pas.
explain.rule: Each other = A → B dan B → A. -selves = subjek ngelakuin ke dirinya sendiri.
explain.memory: Gunakan “each other” saat dua orang saling berinteraksi satu sama lain (hubungan timbal balik dua arah).
explain.avoid: Gambar dua panah di antara orangnya. Dua arah? Pakai “each other”.

items.sentence: If you had told me about the party, I ___.

distractors.misconception: uses second-conditional past simple in an if-clause that needs third-conditional past perfect
distractors.whyFailsId: “would come” ngomongin sekarang atau masa depan yang nggak nyata. Pestanya udah lewat.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk second conditional dipakai buat pengandaian lampau.

distractors.misconception: uses the past simple in the result clause of a third conditional
distractors.whyFailsId: “came” nyatain kejadian lampau nyata, padahal pembicaranya nggak datang.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai past simple di klausa akibat pengandaian lampau, padahal butuh would have + past participle.

distractors.misconception: duplicates 'would' in both clauses
distractors.whyFailsId: “had come” bentuk buat klausa if. Klausa akibat butuh “would have”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk klausa if nyasar ke klausa akibat.

explain.why: Pestanya udah lewat dan pembicara nggak datang, jadi akibat khayalannya pakai “would have come”.
explain.rule: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
explain.memory: Pengandaian lampau: If you had told me, I would have come.
explain.avoid: Past perfect di klausa if? Jawab pakai “would have” plus participle.

items.sentence: These tickets ___ online or at the station.

distractors.misconception: omits the auxiliary 'be' required to form the passive after a modal
distractors.whyFailsId: pasif butuh “be” di antara modal dan participle: can be bought.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu be yang dibutuhin pasif sesudah modal dibuang.

distractors.misconception: leaves the verb in active form after the modal
distractors.whyFailsId: “tickets can buy” bikin tiketnya yang beli. Tiketnya yang dibeli, jadi butuh pasif.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dibiarin aktif sesudah modal.

distractors.misconception: puts 'be' after the past participle in a modal passive
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “be” kata kerjanya harus past participle “bought”, bukan “buy” polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: naruh “be” sesudah past participle, padahal urutannya modal + be + past participle.

explain.why: Tiketnya yang dikenai aksi, jadi pasif modalnya “can be bought”.
explain.rule: Pasif modal: modal + be + past participle (must be signed, can be bought).
explain.memory: Modal pasif itu tiga bagian: can + be + bought.
explain.avoid: Tiga bagian, urutannya selalu: modal, be, participle.

items.sentence: My hair is too long. I'm going to ___ tomorrow.

distractors.misconception: confuses the causative 'have/get' pattern with 'make someone do something'
distractors.whyFailsId: “cut it” artinya aku yang motong sendiri, padahal pembicara pergi ke tukang cukur.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola have/get ketuker sama ngerjain sendiri.

distractors.misconception: uses the -ing form instead of the past participle after 'get'
distractors.whyFailsId: causative butuh past participle “cut”, bukan -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai, bukan past participle.

distractors.misconception: puts 'by' before the person who has the work done
distractors.whyFailsId: objeknya harus sebelum participle, dan “by me” bertentangan sama ide orang lain yang ngerjain.
distractors.misconceptionId: naruh “by” di depan orang yang nyuruh, padahal dia subjeknya, bukan pelakunya.

explain.why: Tukang cukur yang bakal motong, jadi pakai causative “have it cut”.
explain.rule: Causative: have/get + objek + past participle = orang lain yang ngerjain buat kamu.
explain.memory: Pola “have something done” (have it cut) dipakai ketika pekerjaan tersebut dikerjakan oleh orang lain atau ahlinya untuk kita.
explain.avoid: Tanya siapa yang beneran ngerjain. Orang lain? Pakai have + benda + participle.

items.sentence: I have a friend ___ father is a pilot.

distractors.misconception: uses the subject relative pronoun without showing the required possessive relationship
distractors.whyFailsId: “who father” nggak ada hubungan kepemilikan. Ayahnya milik si teman, jadi butuh “whose”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti relatif subjek dipakai tanpa nunjukin kepemilikan.

distractors.misconception: uses 'which' for a person
distractors.whyFailsId: “which” buat benda, dan juga nggak nunjukin kepemilikan.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “which” buat orang, padahal which cuma buat benda atau hewan.

distractors.misconception: confuses the contraction 'who's' (who is / who has) with the possessive relative pronoun 'whose'
distractors.whyFailsId: “who's” artinya “who is”. “A friend who is father” nggak masuk akal.
distractors.misconceptionId: singkatan “who's” (who is) ketuker sama “whose”.

explain.why: Ayahnya itu ayah si teman, jadi kata ganti relatif kepemilikan “whose” yang nyambungin.
explain.rule: Whose + kata benda nunjukin kata benda itu milik orang atau benda yang baru disebut.
explain.memory: “Whose” itu “his/her” di dalam klausa relatif.
explain.avoid: Bisa bilang “his/her/its” di depan kata benda berikutnya? Kata relatifnya “whose”.

items.sentence: ___ she was tired, she finished her homework.

distractors.misconception: puts 'despite' before a full clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “despite” pakai kata benda atau -ing (“despite being tired”), bukan “she was tired”.
distractors.misconceptionId: naruh “despite” di depan klausa utuh, padahal despite cuma buat kata benda atau -ing.

distractors.misconception: Treats 'however' as a subordinating connector that can start a sentence and directly attach to a noun.
distractors.whyFailsId: “however” nyambungin dua kalimat terpisah dan diikuti koma. Nggak bisa ngegabung dua klausa dalam satu kalimat begini.
distractors.misconceptionId: “however” dianggap bisa buka kalimat dan langsung nyambung ke klausa.

distractors.misconception: uses 'but' as a subordinating connector at the start of the sentence
distractors.whyFailsId: “but” ngegabung klausa di tengah kalimat, bukan di paling depan sebelum klausa berkoma.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “but” di awal kalimat buat ngegabung dua klausa, padahal but cuma nyambung di tengah.

explain.why: “She was tired” klausa utuh, jadi penghubung pertentangannya harus “although”.
explain.rule: Although + klausa. Despite + kata benda/-ing. However + koma, buka kalimat baru.
explain.memory: Although ketemu klausa, despite ketemu kata benda: although she was… / despite being…
explain.avoid: Lihat yang ngikut sesudah titik-titik: subjek + kata kerja berarti “although”.

items.sentence: It was ___ good film that we watched it twice.

distractors.misconception: uses 'so' before a noun phrase with an adjective
distractors.whyFailsId: “so” di depan kata sifat aja (“so good”). Di depan “good film” katanya “such a”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “so” di depan kata sifat + kata benda, padahal di situ butuh “such”.

distractors.misconception: drops the article after 'such' before a singular noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “film” tunggal dan bisa dihitung, jadi butuh “a” sesudah “such”.
distractors.misconceptionId: ngilangin “a” sesudah such, padahal kata benda tunggalnya butuh artikel.

distractors.misconception: Inserts an article as if a noun were about to follow.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so” nggak pernah diikuti artikel. Pola sama kata benda itu “such a”.
distractors.misconceptionId: artikel disisipin seolah ada kata benda yang ngikut so.

explain.why: “Good film” itu kata sifat + kata benda tunggal, jadi struktur akibatnya pakai “such a … that”.
explain.rule: So + kata sifat … that. Such (a/an) + kata sifat + kata benda … that.
explain.memory: So ketemu kata sifat aja, such a ketemu kata sifat + kata benda: so good / such a good film.
explain.avoid: Ada kata benda sesudah kata sifatnya? Ya → such (a). Nggak → so.

items.sentence: I was very tired, so I didn't do ___ last night.

distractors.misconception: using a positive indefinite pronoun that contradicts the negative context
distractors.whyFailsId: “didn't” udah negatif, jadi “nothing” bikin negatif dobel.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti positif dipasang padahal konteksnya negatif.

distractors.misconception: uses 'anything' in a positive clause that has no negative word to license it
distractors.whyFailsId: “something” buat kalimat positif. Sesudah “didn't” katanya “anything”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “anything” dipasang di kalimat positif tanpa kata negatif sama sekali.

distractors.misconception: leaves bare 'any' without a noun in a positive clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “any” butuh kata benda sesudahnya (“any work”). Sendirian nggak bisa jadi objek “do”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “any” polos ditaruh tanpa nomina di kalimat positif.

explain.why: “Didn't do” udah negatif, jadi objeknya “anything”: didn't do anything.
explain.rule: Kata kerja negatif + anything. Kata kerja positif + something. “Nothing” cuma sama kata kerja positif (I did nothing).
explain.memory: Didn't … anything / did … nothing.
explain.avoid: Ada “not” atau “n't” di kata kerjanya? Kata gabungannya mulai dari any-.

items.sentence: My bike ___ last night. I have no idea who did it.

distractors.misconception: active voice used despite an unknown/irrelevant agent
distractors.whyFailsId: “my bike stole” bikin sepedanya jadi pencuri. Sepedanya yang kena aksi, jadi butuh pasif.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimat aktif dipakai padahal pelakunya nggak diketahui.

distractors.misconception: malformed passive/perfect blend
distractors.whyFailsId: “has stole” nyampur kata bantu perfect sama bentuk past simple. Bentuk maupun waktunya nggak cocok.
distractors.misconceptionId: campuran pasif dan perfect yang bentuknya rusak.

distractors.misconception: adds a vague, uninformative agent instead of omitting it
distractors.whyFailsId: “by someone” nggak nambah apa-apa. Kalimat berikutnya udah bilang nggak ada yang tahu pelakunya.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelaku samar malah ditambahin, padahal mestinya dihilangin.

explain.why: Pencurinya nggak diketahui, jadi pasif “was stolen” fokus ke sepedanya dan pelakunya nggak disebut.
explain.rule: Pasif tanpa pelaku: be + past participle, kalau pelakunya nggak diketahui, udah jelas, atau nggak penting.
explain.memory: Pelaku nggak diketahui → was stolen (tanpa “by”).
explain.avoid: Tanya: kita tahu atau peduli siapa pelakunya? Kalau nggak, pakai pasif dan berhenti di participle.

items.sentence: Ali said, "I live in Surabaya." → Ali said he ___ in Surabaya.

distractors.misconception: no backshift applied
distractors.whyFailsId: “said” lampau, jadi “lives” harus mundur jadi “lived”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pergeseran bentuk waktunya nggak dilakuin sama sekali.

distractors.misconception: backshift target confused with present perfect
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple mundur ke past simple, bukan ke present perfect.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sasaran gesernya ketuker sama present perfect.

distractors.misconception: tense category changed instead of shifted one step back
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” itu mundurnya “will”. Kalimat aslinya nggak ada “will”.
distractors.misconceptionId: jenis bentuk waktunya ganti, bukan mundur satu langkah.

explain.why: Sesudah kata pelapor lampau “said”, present simple “live” mundur satu langkah jadi “lived”.
explain.rule: Mundur: present simple → past simple; will → would; present perfect → past perfect.
explain.memory: Live → lived sesudah said.
explain.avoid: Cari kata kerja aslinya, lalu geser tepat satu langkah ke lampau.

items.sentence: "Don't touch the wet paint," Mum said. → Mum told us ___ the wet paint.

distractors.misconception: applies the statement-reporting pattern ('that' clause) to an imperative
distractors.whyFailsId: perintah dilaporin pakai infinitive, bukan klausa “that”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola pelaporan pernyataan dipakai buat sebuah perintah.

distractors.misconception: backshifts as if reporting a past statement rather than a command
distractors.whyFailsId: “didn't touch” laporin apa yang terjadi, bukan apa yang Ibu perintahin.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dimundurin kayak ngelaporin pernyataan lampau, bukan perintah.

distractors.misconception: leaves the original imperative form unchanged, without integrating it into reported speech
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk perintah langsung nggak bisa ditempel sesudah “told us”. Butuh “not to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk perintah aslinya dibiarin utuh tanpa dimasukin ke pelaporan.

explain.why: Larangan jadi “told + orang + not to + kata kerja”: told us not to touch.
explain.rule: Perintah yang dilaporin: tell/ask + objek + (not) to + kata kerja dasar.
explain.memory: Perintah “Don't touch” dilaporin jadi “told us not to touch”.
explain.avoid: Denger perintah? Susun ulang jadi “told someone (not) to do”.

items.sentence: What a view! ___ it beautiful here?

distractors.misconception: uses a neutral positive question form, missing the speaker's implied surprise/assumption
distractors.whyFailsId: “Is it beautiful?” pertanyaan datar. Pembicaranya jelas udah berpikir begitu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk pertanyaan positif yang netral dipakai, jadi rasa herannya ilang.

distractors.misconception: uses the 'be' auxiliary instead of the 'do' auxiliary needed for the main verb 'sleep'
distractors.whyFailsId: “beautiful” kata sifat sesudah “be”, jadi kata bantunya “is”, bukan “does”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu be dipakai buat kata kerja utama yang butuh do.

distractors.misconception: uses present-tense negative auxiliary in a context that requires the past tense to match 'last night'
distractors.whyFailsId: pemandangannya ada di depan mereka sekarang, jadi “wasn't” yang lampau nggak cocok.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu negatif bentuk present dipakai padahal konteksnya lampau.

explain.why: Pembicara kagum sama pemandangannya dan ngarep setuju, jadi pakai pertanyaan negatif “Isn't it beautiful?”.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan negatif (Isn't / Don't / Didn't …?) = pembicara ngarep jawaban “ya”.
explain.memory: Pertanyaan negatif seperti “Isn't it beautiful?” dipakai untuk meminta persetujuan saat kita yakin lawan bicara juga sependapat.
explain.avoid: Udah yakin dan cuma mau diajak setuju? Mulai dari kata bantu negatif.

items.sentence: On Friday Dina said, "I'll call you tomorrow." A week later: Dina said she would call me ___.

distractors.misconception: leaving the original deictic time word unchanged despite the shift in reporting time
distractors.whyFailsId: “tomorrow” bakal berarti sehari sesudah laporan, bukan hari Sabtu yang Dina maksud.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata waktu aslinya dibiarin utuh padahal waktu pelaporannya udah beda.

distractors.misconception: misreading the original 'today' as if it referred to the day after speaking
distractors.whyFailsId: “yesterday” nunjuk ke belakang dari sekarang. Dina ngomongin hari sesudah Jumat.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata “today” dibaca kayak nunjuk hari setelah dia ngomong.

distractors.misconception: producing an incomplete deictic shift missing the demonstrative
distractors.whyFailsId: frasanya butuh “the”: the next day / the following day.
distractors.misconceptionId: gesernya belum lengkap karena kata penunjuknya ilang.

explain.why: Laporannya dibuat seminggu kemudian, jadi “tomorrow” geser jadi “the next day”.
explain.rule: Geseran waktu di kalimat laporan: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before.
explain.memory: Tomorrow → the next day.
explain.avoid: Tanya: “tomorrow” masih nunjuk hari yang sama dari hari ini? Kalau nggak, geser.

items.sentence: The museum ___ at 9 a.m. every day, so let's be there early.

distractors.misconception: using present continuous, associated with personal arrangements, for a fixed external timetable
distractors.whyFailsId: present continuous buat janji pribadi, bukan jam resmi harian.
distractors.misconceptionId: present continuous yang lekat sama janji pribadi dipakai buat jadwal resmi.

distractors.misconception: using 'going to' for intention/prediction rather than an externally fixed schedule
distractors.whyFailsId: “going to” nunjukin niat atau perkiraan. Jadwal tetap cukup dinyatain sebagai fakta.
distractors.misconceptionId: “going to” yang nyatain niat atau ramalan dipakai buat jadwal resmi.

distractors.misconception: using future perfect, which describes completion before a reference point, not the scheduled departure itself
distractors.whyFailsId: future perfect artinya “selesai sebelum suatu titik”. Kalimatnya ngasih jam buka rutin.
distractors.misconceptionId: future perfect dipakai padahal bentuk itu nyebut kelar sebelum satu titik acuan.

explain.why: “Every day” dan jam resminya bikin ini jadwal tetap, jadi pakai present simple “opens”.
explain.rule: Present simple buat jadwal tetap: “the train leaves”, “the museum opens”, “the class starts”.
explain.memory: Jadwal → present simple.
explain.avoid: Tercetak di jadwal atau papan? Pakai present simple.

items.sentence: "I will help you move," Rio said. → Rio said he ___ help me move.

distractors.misconception: Assumes modals don't need to shift in reported speech.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “said” yang lampau, “will” biasanya mundur jadi “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal dikira nggak perlu ikut digeser di kalimat pelaporan.

distractors.misconception: Treats the modal as a regular verb that takes -s for third person.
distractors.whyFailsId: modal nggak pernah pakai -s. “Wills” nganggap “will” kayak kata kerja biasa.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal diperlakuin kayak kata kerja biasa yang nerima akhiran -s.

distractors.misconception: Attempts to stack two modals together.
distractors.whyFailsId: modal langsung diikuti kata kerja dasar. Nggak ada “to” sesudah “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: dua modal ditumpuk berjajar.

explain.why: Janjinya dilaporin di masa lampau, jadi “will” jadi “would”: said he would help.
explain.rule: Mundurnya modal: will → would, can → could, may → might. Modal nggak pakai -s dan nggak pakai “to”.
explain.memory: Will → would sesudah said.
explain.avoid: Ada modal di kalimat langsungnya? Tuker sama pasangan lampaunya dan kata kerjanya tetap polos.

items.sentence: "Are you hungry?" she asked. → She asked me ___ hungry.

distractors.misconception: keeps direct-question inversion and omits if/whether
distractors.whyFailsId: masih urutan pertanyaan dan nggak ada “if” buat ngenalin pertanyaan yang dilaporin.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembalikan khas pertanyaan langsung dipertahanin dan pembukanya dihilangin.

distractors.misconception: uses 'that' for a yes/no reported question
distractors.whyFailsId: “that” buat laporin kalimat berita. Pertanyaan ya/tidak butuh “if” atau “whether”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “that” dipakai buat pertanyaan “yes” atau “no” yang dilaporin.

distractors.misconception: adds whether but retains auxiliary-subject inversion
distractors.whyFailsId: “if” udah bener, tapi subjeknya harus sebelum kata kerja: if I was.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembukanya udah bener tapi pembalikan kata bantunya dipertahanin.

explain.why: Pertanyaan ya/tidak dilaporin pakai “if” plus urutan kalimat berita, dan “are” mundur jadi “was”.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan ya/tidak yang dilaporin: asked + if/whether + subjek + kata kerja (dimundurin).
explain.memory: Pertanyaan “Are you…?” dilaporin jadi “asked if I was…”.
explain.avoid: Pertanyaan langsungnya bisa dijawab ya atau tidak? Mulai laporannya pakai “if”.

items.sentence: Grandpa is in ___ after his operation, so we visit him every evening.

distractors.misconception: focuses on a particular building instead of institutional attendance
distractors.whyFailsId: “the hospital” nunjuk gedungnya. Dirawat sebagai pasien nggak pakai artikel.
distractors.misconceptionId: perhatian dialihin ke satu gedung tertentu, bukan ke kegiatan belajarnya.

distractors.misconception: introduces one unspecified building rather than the attendance idiom
distractors.whyFailsId: “a hospital” ngenalin satu gedung sembarang, bukan rawat inap Kakek.
distractors.misconceptionId: satu gedung yang nggak jelas dikenalin, bukan ungkapan kegiatan belajarnya.

distractors.misconception: turns one routine of attendance into a generic plural destination
distractors.whyFailsId: “hospitals” yang jamak bikin satu rawat inap jadi tujuan umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: satu kebiasaan belajar diubah jadi tujuan jamak yang umum.

explain.why: Kakek di sana sebagai pasien, jadi “in hospital” tanpa artikel.
explain.rule: Tanpa artikel kalau lembaganya dipakai sesuai fungsi: in hospital, at school, in prison. Pakai “the” buat gedungnya.
explain.memory: Frasa “in hospital” (tanpa “the”) berarti sedang dirawat sebagai pasien. Jika hanya berkunjung, gunakan “at the hospital”.
explain.avoid: Tanya: pasien, murid, atau tahanan? Kalau ya, buang artikelnya.

items.sentence: The film ___ we watched last night was really boring.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal relative pronoun for a non-human antecedent.
distractors.whyFailsId: “who” buat orang. Film butuh “that” atau “which”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penghubung buat orang dipakai pada kata benda yang bukan orang.

distractors.misconception: uses possessive 'whose' where the clause needs an object relative pronoun or nothing at all
distractors.whyFailsId: “whose” nunjukin kepemilikan. Di sini nggak ada yang punya apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kepemilikan “whose” dipasang padahal nggak ada makna punya-punyaan di kalimatnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'what' as a relative pronoun, a common cross-linguistic transfer error.
distractors.whyFailsId: “what” nggak pernah jadi kata ganti relatif sesudah kata benda di bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: “what” dipakai sebagai kata penghubung, kekeliruan yang lazim kebawa dari bahasa lain.

explain.why: “The film” itu benda dan objek dari “watched”, jadi “that” pas, bahkan bisa dibuang.
explain.rule: Kata ganti relatif objek buat benda: that / which, atau nggak ada sama sekali: the film (that) we watched.
explain.memory: Kata gantinya bisa hilang: “the film (that) we watched”.
explain.avoid: Coba hapus kata gantinya. Kalau kalimatnya masih jalan, “that” atau kosong yang bener.

items.sentence: The test was ___ easier than I expected.

distractors.misconception: Transfers the common absolute-adjective intensifier 'very' onto a comparative form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “very” di depan kata sifat biasa (very easy), bukan di depan “easier”.
distractors.misconceptionId: penguat kata sifat biasa kebawa ke bentuk perbandingan.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'so', which needs a following 'that'-clause or exclamatory context, as a plain intensifier before a comparative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so” butuh klausa “that” atau kalimat seru, dan nggak nempel ke “easier”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “so” yang minta anak kalimat akibat dipakai sebagai penguat biasa.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'too' (meaning excessive) as if it were a neutral intensifier.
distractors.whyFailsId: “too” artinya “lebih dari yang baik” dan nggak bisa nguatin bentuk banding.
distractors.misconceptionId: “too” yang berarti berlebihan dipakai seolah penguat yang netral.

explain.why: “Easier” bentuk banding, jadi penguatnya penguat bentuk banding: a lot easier.
explain.rule: Di depan bentuk banding pakai much, far, a lot, atau a bit; jangan very.
explain.memory: Very easy, tapi a lot easier.
explain.avoid: Lihat -er atau “more”? Ambil much / far / a lot.

items.sentence: A: "My brother is moving to Iceland." B: "He's moving ___?"

distractors.misconception: Forms a standard inverted question instead of echoing the statement's structure.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngubah gemanya jadi pertanyaan biasa yang kebalik dan ngulang subjeknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: pertanyaan terbalik yang baku disusun, bukan ngulang susunan pernyataannya.

distractors.misconception: Fully reformulates the question with standard word order rather than echoing.
distractors.whyFailsId: bikin ulang seluruh pertanyaan, bukan ngulang bagian yang bikin kaget.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya disusun ulang sepenuhnya, bukan diulang.

distractors.misconception: Uses a gerund fragment instead of the statement's original verb form.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngulang potongan kata kerjanya. Gemanya udah punya “He's moving” sebelum titik-titik.
distractors.misconceptionId: penggalan bentuk -ing dipakai menggantikan bentuk kata kerja aslinya.

explain.why: Pertanyaan gema ngikutin urutan pernyataan dan ngeganti bagian yang bikin kaget sama “where”: He's moving where?
explain.rule: Pertanyaan gema: ulangi pernyataannya, taruh kata tanya di posisi info yang bikin kaget, nada naik.
explain.memory: He's moving where?
explain.avoid: Salin kalimatnya, lalu taruh kata tanya persis di tempat kata yang bikin kaget.

items.sentence: It's only the 10th, and I ___ two books this month already.

distractors.misconception: Uses past simple because a specific number of emails is mentioned.
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple nutup periodenya, padahal “this month” masih jalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipakai padahal rentang waktunya belum tutup.

distractors.misconception: Uses past continuous to describe a series of completed actions.
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous nunjukin aksi yang lagi jalan, bukan dua buku yang udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: past continuous dipakai buat nggambarin serangkaian tindakan yang udah tuntas.

distractors.misconception: Uses present simple, ignoring that the sentence reports completed past actions within the current period.
distractors.whyFailsId: present continuous artinya sekarang ini. “Already” nunjukin bukunya udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: present simple dipakai padahal kalimatnya nyebut tindakan lampau tertentu.

explain.why: “This month” belum berakhir, jadi aksi yang selesai di dalamnya pakai present perfect: have read.
explain.rule: Present perfect sama periode yang belum selesai: today, this week, this month, this year.
explain.memory: This month (masih terbuka) → have read.
explain.avoid: Tanya: periode waktunya masih terbuka? Kalau ya, pakai have/has + past participle.

items.sentence: After the course, you ___ speak basic Korean.

distractors.misconception: places the finite modal 'can' after infinitive 'to'
distractors.whyFailsId: “can” itu modal berkonjugasi dan nggak bisa ngikut “will”.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bertense ditaruh sesudah “to”.

distractors.misconception: uses a finite past/conditional modal in a non-finite slot
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” juga modal berkonjugasi. Dua modal nggak pernah ditumpuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bertense lampau dipakai di posisi yang minta bentuk tanpa tense.

distractors.misconception: uses a gerund-participle where a bare infinitive is required
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “will” kata kerjanya bentuk polos “be”, bukan “being”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai di posisi yang minta bentuk dasar.

explain.why: “Will” udah ngisi slot modal, jadi kemampuannya pakai “be able to”: will be able to speak.
explain.rule: Kemampuan sesudah modal lain atau “to”: pakai be able to (will be able to, hope to be able to).
explain.memory: Will + be able to.
explain.avoid: Butuh “can” sesudah will, must, atau to? Tuker sama “be able to”.

items.sentence: I called three friends, but ___ them answered.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' before the object pronoun
distractors.whyFailsId: di depan kata ganti kayak “them”, “none” butuh “of”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin di depan kata ganti objek.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and ignores the explicitly two-person set
distractors.whyFailsId: “no” langsung di depan kata benda (no friends), nggak pernah di depan “them”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin sekaligus ngabaikan bahwa kelompoknya jelas dua orang.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and reverses the affirmative meaning
distractors.whyFailsId: “any of them answered” nggak negatif. Kalimatnya butuh “none of”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin sekaligus ngebalik makna kalimatnya jadi negatif.

explain.why: Nggak ada yang ngangkat, dan “them” itu kata ganti, jadi bentuknya “none of them”.
explain.rule: Penanda jumlah + of + kata ganti objek: none of them, both of us, all of you, some of it.
explain.memory: Di depan kata ganti selalu ada “of”: “none of them”, “both of us”.
explain.avoid: Ada them / us / you / it sesudah penanda jumlahnya? Selipin “of”.

items.sentence: These shoes are too small. Do you have any bigger ___?

distractors.misconception: picks plural 'ones' to replace a single noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “shoes” jamak, jadi penggantinya harus “ones” yang jamak.
distractors.misconceptionId: “ones” jamak dipakai buat gantiin satu benda doang.

distractors.misconception: uses definite 'it' after 'a new' where the indefinite substitute 'one' is needed
distractors.whyFailsId: “them” nggak bisa ngikut kata sifat kayak “bigger”. Dia berdiri sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: “it” yang definit dipasang sesudah “a new”, padahal slotnya minta pengganti tak tentu “one”.

distractors.misconception: repeats the replaced noun and stacks the substitute 'one' after it
distractors.whyFailsId: ngulang kata bendanya dan nambah pengganti di atasnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: nominanya diulang terus masih ditumpuk lagi sama pengganti “one”.

explain.why: “Ones” ngegantiin “shoes” yang jamak sesudah kata sifat “bigger”: any bigger ones.
explain.rule: Kata sifat + one (tunggal) / ones (jamak) ngegantiin kata benda yang udah disebut.
explain.memory: Gunakan kata “ones” sesudah kata sifat untuk menggantikan kata benda jamak yang sudah disebut sebelumnya (“bigger shoes”).
explain.avoid: Hitung kata benda yang diganti: satu → one, banyak → ones.

items.sentence: Oh no, I forgot ___ the door when I left this morning!

distractors.misconception: applies the 'future duty' pattern ('remember to do') to a sentence that is actually recalling a completed past action
distractors.whyFailsId: “forget locking” artinya aku nggak ingat pernah ngunci. Di sini nguncinya nggak pernah terjadi.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola kewajiban nanti dipakai buat kalimat yang lagi inget kejadian lampau.

distractors.misconception: uses the bare infinitive, which isn't a valid pattern after 'remember' in either meaning
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja polos nggak bisa ngikut “forget”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai padahal bukan pola yang sah sesudah “remember”.

distractors.misconception: applies a perfect to-infinitive after 'remember', which English does not use for recalling a past action
distractors.whyFailsId: perfect infinitive nggak dipakai sesudah “forget” buat tugas biasa yang kelewat.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk to sempurna dipasang ke “remember”, padahal buat ingatan lampau pola itu nggak dipakai.

explain.why: Pintunya nggak pernah dikunci, jadi “forget to lock” (tugas yang nggak dikerjain) maknanya yang dibutuhin.
explain.rule: Forget/remember + to-infinitive = kewajiban. Forget/remember + -ing = ingatan soal yang udah terjadi.
explain.memory: Pola “forget + to do” (forgot to lock) berarti lupa melakukan sesuatu sehingga pekerjaan itu tidak terlaksana.
explain.avoid: Tanya: aksinya terjadi? Kalau nggak, pakai “forget to”.

items.sentence: Phones are getting ___ every year.

distractors.misconception: treats a continuous, ongoing change as a single fixed-point comparison
distractors.whyFailsId: “than” butuh hal kedua buat dibandingin. Di sini nggak ada yang ngikut.
distractors.misconceptionId: perubahan yang jalan terus diperlakuin sebagai perbandingan di satu titik aja.

distractors.misconception: confuses a progressive change over time with a superlative ranking among multiple items
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk paling nyebut yang teratas. Nggak bisa nunjukin perubahan “every year”.
distractors.misconceptionId: perubahan yang jalan ketuker sama peringkat superlative di antara banyak hal.

distractors.misconception: uses a single comparative with 'more' for a short adjective, and frames it as a comparison to a norm rather than ongoing change
distractors.whyFailsId: “expensive” kata sifat panjang, jadi pakai “more”, bukan -er.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai satu bentuk “more” buat kata sifat pendek, dan dibingkai sebagai perbandingan sama kebiasaan.

explain.why: “Every year” nunjukin kenaikan terus-menerus, jadi bentuk banding ganda “more and more expensive” pas.
explain.rule: Perubahan bertahap: -er and -er (bigger and bigger) atau more and more + kata sifat panjang.
explain.memory: More and more expensive every year.
explain.avoid: Masih berubah? Gandakan bentuk bandingnya.

items.sentence: ___ that this old house is haunted, but I don't believe it.

distractors.misconception: using active voice with a vague 'they' plus an incorrect continuous form for a general belief
distractors.whyFailsId: “they” yang samar dalam bentuk -ing nggak laporin keyakinan umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk aktif dengan “they” yang samar dipakai bareng bentuk continuous yang keliru.

distractors.misconception: treating 'it' as an active subject capable of believing
distractors.whyFailsId: “it says” bikin “it” jadi pembicara. Rumahnya nggak ngomong apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: “it” diperlakuin sebagai subjek pelaku yang bisa meyakini sesuatu.

distractors.misconception: dropping the required dummy subject 'it' from the impersonal passive pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: pasif impersonal butuh subjek semu “it” di depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: subjek semu “it” yang diwajibin pola ini dihilangin.

explain.why: Nggak ada sumber tertentu, jadi pasif impersonal “It is said that…” yang dipakai.
explain.rule: Pelaporan impersonal susunannya “It” + “is/was” + “said/believed/thought” + “that” + klausa.
explain.memory: Rumor atau keyakinan umum dibuka pakai “It is said that…”.
explain.avoid: Laporin rumor atau keyakinan umum? Mulai dari “It is said / believed that”.

items.sentence: The results are expected ___ on Friday.

distractors.misconception: using active infinitive when the subject (the policy) cannot perform the announcing itself
distractors.whyFailsId: hasilnya nggak bisa nerbitin apa-apa. Hasilnya yang diterbitin, jadi butuh pasif.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk to aktif dipakai padahal subjeknya nggak mungkin ngumumin sendiri.

distractors.misconception: using a gerund where an infinitive pattern after 'expected' is required
distractors.whyFailsId: “expected” pakai to-infinitive, bukan -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai padahal sesudah “expected” yang diminta pola bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: adding continuous aspect to the passive infinitive unnecessarily
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing nambah makna berlangsung yang nggak cocok buat satu kali terbit.
distractors.misconceptionId: makna berkelanjutan ditambahin ke bentuk to pasif tanpa perlu.

explain.why: Hasilnya yang kena aksi, jadi sesudah “expected” pakai infinitive pasif “to be published”.
explain.rule: Be expected / supposed / likely + to be + past participle kalau subjeknya yang dikenai aksi.
explain.memory: Expected to be published.
explain.avoid: Tanya: subjeknya ngelakuin aksi atau kena aksi? Kena → to be + participle.

items.sentence: The box was heavy, but I tried ___ it alone. I couldn't.

distractors.misconception: using 'try to' (make a difficult effort) where 'try -ing' (experiment with a solution) is meant
distractors.whyFailsId: “try lifting” artinya nyoba ngangkat sebagai salah satu cara. Di sini pembicaranya berusaha keras dan gagal.
distractors.misconceptionId: “try to” yang berarti usaha keras dipakai padahal maksudnya nyoba satu cara.

distractors.misconception: using the bare infinitive after 'try', which isn't a valid pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja polos nggak bisa ngikut “try”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai sesudah “try” padahal itu bukan pola yang sah.

distractors.misconception: using a perfect gerund, implying the action is already completed
distractors.whyFailsId: perfect gerund bilang ngangkatnya udah selesai, bertentangan sama “I couldn't”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing perfect dipakai jadi tindakannya seolah udah kelar.

explain.why: Ngangkat kotaknya usaha keras yang gagal, jadi “tried to lift” maknanya yang dibutuhin.
explain.rule: Try + to-infinitive = berusaha (sulit). Try + -ing = nyoba satu cara buat lihat hasilnya.
explain.memory: Tried to lift (usaha) vs. try restarting (cara).
explain.avoid: Sulit dan mungkin nggak bisa? Pakai “try to”.

items.sentence: We ___ the early train, but we chose to sleep in. No regrets!

distractors.misconception: Confuses missed opportunity with retrospective advice/criticism.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should have” ngeritik kesalahan, padahal pembicaranya bilang “no regrets”.
distractors.misconceptionId: peluang yang terlewat ketuker sama nasihat atau teguran sesudah kejadian.

distractors.misconception: Confuses expressing a past possibility with reporting a completed achieved ability.
distractors.whyFailsId: “were able to” laporin kita beneran ngejar keretanya, padahal nggak.
distractors.misconceptionId: nyatain kemungkinan lampau ketuker sama laporan kemampuan yang kelaksana.

distractors.misconception: Uses present modal for a past hypothetical situation.
distractors.whyFailsId: “can” bentuk sekarang. Kereta yang kelewat itu di masa lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bentuk present dipakai buat keadaan lampau yang cuma dibayangin.

explain.why: Ngejar keretanya mungkin tapi nggak terjadi, dan nggak ada kritik, jadi “could have caught” pas.
explain.rule: Could have + past participle = kemungkinan lampau yang nggak dipakai. Should have = kritik.
explain.memory: Could have, tapi nggak.
explain.avoid: Tanya: mungkin tapi nggak dilakuin, dan nggak ada yang disalahin? Pakai “could have”.

items.sentence: My aunt works as a nurse in ___ Philippines.

distractors.misconception: Treats the country name as an ordinary countable noun needing an indefinite article.
distractors.whyFailsId: nama negara bukan kata benda yang bisa dihitung pakai “a”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nama negara diperlakukan sebagai kata benda terhitung biasa yang butuh artikel tak tentu.

distractors.misconception: Applies the indefinite article rule based on the following vowel sound, ignoring that country names don't take indefinite articles at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: “an” dipilih dari bunyi vokal sesudahnya, tapi artikel tak tentu mana pun nggak cocok buat nama negara.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan artikel tak tentu diterapkan berdasarkan bunyi vokal, tanpa melihat bahwa nama negara memang tidak memakainya.

distractors.misconception: Overgeneralizes the common 'no article before country names' rule to every country name.
distractors.whyFailsId: kebanyakan negara tanpa artikel, tapi nama jamak kayak the Philippines dan the Netherlands butuh “the”.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan umum tanpa artikel di depan nama negara diberlakukan untuk semua nama negara.

explain.why: “Philippines” nama negara jamak, jadi pakai “the”: the Philippines.
explain.rule: Tanpa artikel buat kebanyakan negara (Japan, Indonesia). “The” buat nama jamak atau deskriptif (the Philippines, the United States, the UK).
explain.memory: Nama negara jamak pakai “the”: “the Philippines”, “the Netherlands”.
explain.avoid: Nama negaranya berakhiran -s atau ada kata kayak States/Kingdom/Republic? Pakai “the”.

items.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ his sudden decision to leave.

distractors.misconception: Assumes 'of' universally links a noun to what it relates to.
distractors.whyFailsId: “of” kerasa wajar karena nyambungin banyak kata benda, tapi “reason” pakai “for”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dikira selalu bisa nyambungin kata benda sama hal yang berkaitan.

distractors.misconception: Transfers the preposition pattern from a related phrase like 'search for' onto 'solution'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” punya “solution to” atau “answer to”, bukan “reason”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola kata depan dari ungkapan berkaitan kayak “search for” dibawa ke “solution”.

distractors.misconception: Borrows a preposition associated with 'deal with' or 'cope with' a problem.
distractors.whyFailsId: “about” ngenalin topik. “Reason” butuh penanda sebab “for”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan yang lekat di “deal with” dipinjem buat “solution”.

explain.why: Kata benda “reason” selalu diikuti “for”: the reason for his decision.
explain.rule: Pasangan tetap kata benda + kata depan: reason for, solution to, answer to, effect on.
explain.memory: Reason for, solution to.
explain.avoid: Simpan kata benda sama kata depannya sebagai satu paket: reason for.

items.sentence: If only I ___ harder for the exam last week!

distractors.misconception: staying with the past simple, which cannot mark the unreal past that regret needs
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple sesudah “if only” buat harapan sekarang. “Last week” bikin ini penyesalan lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipertahanin buat penyesalan lampau.

distractors.misconception: moving the 'would have' shape of the result clause into the wish clause itself
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have” bentuk klausa akibat. Nggak ngikut “if only”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk klausa hasil dipindah ke klausa harapan.

distractors.misconception: choosing the present perfect, which ties the missed reading to the present moment
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect ngiket belajarnya ke sekarang, padahal “last week” udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: present perfect dipilih buat kejadian yang udah ketutup.

explain.why: Ujiannya minggu lalu, jadi penyesalannya pakai past perfect: If only I had studied harder.
explain.rule: If only / I wish + past perfect = penyesalan soal lampau. + past simple = harapan soal sekarang.
explain.memory: Udah terlambat buat disesali: “If only I had…”.
explain.avoid: Ada kata waktu lampau sama “if only”? Mundur satu langkah lagi: had + participle.

items.sentence: My neighbour plays loud music every night. I wish he ___ it down.

distractors.misconception: treats a complaint about repeated behaviour as a wished-for state with wish + past simple
distractors.whyFailsId: “wish + past simple” ngegambarin keadaan. Keluhan soal kelakuan berulang pakai “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: keluhan soal kebiasaan orang lain dibungkus “wish + past simple”.

distractors.misconception: keeping the present tense after 'wish', reading the situation as a real current fact
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk sekarang nggak bisa ngikut “wish”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang dipertahanin sesudah “wish”.

distractors.misconception: puts future 'will' after 'wish', calquing Indonesian 'akan'
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” nggak pernah ngikut “wish”. Bentuknya “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “will” dipasang sesudah “wish” karena kebawa makna “akan”.

explain.why: Pembicara kesal sama kebiasaan tetangganya dan mau itu berubah, jadi pakai “wish he would turn”.
explain.rule: Wish + would + kata kerja dasar = kesal sama kelakuan orang lain yang bisa dia ubah.
explain.memory: Kesal sama kelakuan orang lain: “I wish he would stop!”.
explain.avoid: Ngeluh soal yang terus dilakuin orang lain? “I wish they would…”

items.sentence: It took me a month to get used to ___ up at five for work.

distractors.misconception: reads the 'to' in 'be used to' as an infinitive marker, copying the past-habit pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” di “get used to” itu kata depan, jadi kata kerja sesudahnya pakai -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: “to” di “be used to” dibaca sebagai penanda infinitive.

distractors.misconception: slots a finite past form after the preposition 'to' in 'be used to'
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau nggak bisa ngikut kata depan “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau ditaruh sesudah preposisi “to” karena kebawa rasa lampau “used to”.

distractors.misconception: inserts infinitive 'be' after 'used to' although this 'to' is a preposition needing -ing
distractors.whyFailsId: “be” nganggap “to” penanda infinitive. Polanya butuh -ing langsung.
distractors.misconceptionId: “be” infinitive diselipin sesudah “used to”, padahal “to”-nya preposisi.

explain.why: “Get used to” diikuti -ing: get used to getting up at five.
explain.rule: Be/get used to + -ing = terbiasa / jadi terbiasa. Used to + kata kerja dasar = kebiasaan lampau.
explain.memory: Get used to getting up early.
explain.avoid: Ada “be” atau “get” sebelum “used to”? Kata kerja berikutnya berakhiran -ing.

items.sentence: I'd rather ___ tea than coffee in the evening.

distractors.misconception: generalizes the to-infinitive to 'would rather' on the model of 'prefer to'
distractors.whyFailsId: “prefer to drink” pakai “to”, tapi “would rather” pakai kata kerja polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would rather” ikut-ikutan pola “prefer to”, jadi ketambahan “to”.

distractors.misconception: imports the gerund complement of 'prefer' into the 'would rather' pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: -ing punya “prefer drinking”, bukan “would rather”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap -ing punya “prefer” dibawa ke pola “would rather”.

distractors.misconception: backshifts to a past form after 'would rather' although no second subject intervenes
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau nggak dipakai sesudah “would rather” kalau pembicara ngomongin kesukaannya sendiri sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya digeser ke bentuk lampau padahal nggak ada subjek kedua.

explain.why: “Would rather” langsung diikuti kata kerja dasar: I'd rather drink tea.
explain.rule: Would rather + kata kerja dasar (+ than + kata kerja dasar). Prefer + to-infinitive atau -ing.
explain.memory: Sesudah “would rather” kata kerjanya polos: “I'd rather drink tea than coffee”.
explain.avoid: Sesudah “rather”, tulis kata kerjanya tanpa apa pun di depannya.

items.sentence: Dani ___ meet us at six, but he never showed up.

distractors.misconception: drops the obligatory 'be' before 'supposed to'
distractors.whyFailsId: “supposed to” selalu butuh bentuk “be” di depannya: was supposed to.
distractors.misconceptionId: “be” di depan “supposed to” dihilangin, kebawa kalimat Indonesia yang nggak butuh kata penghubung.

distractors.misconception: treats 'suppose' as an ordinary present-tense verb instead of the passive pattern 'be supposed to'
distractors.whyFailsId: “suppose” sebagai kata kerja biasa artinya “mengira”. Pola harapan butuh “be supposed to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “suppose” dipakai kayak kata kerja kini biasa, padahal maknanya cuma ada di pola pasif “be supposed to”.

distractors.misconception: forces a progressive onto the fixed passive participle 'supposed'
distractors.whyFailsId: “supposed” di sini participle tetap dan nggak pernah pakai -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: participle beku “supposed” dipaksa jadi bentuk -ing.

explain.why: Ketemu jam enam itu janjinya, dan gagal, jadi “was supposed to meet” nyatain harapan yang nggak terpenuhi.
explain.rule: Be supposed to + kata kerja = yang diharapkan atau dijanjikan. “Be”-nya berubah ngikut waktu (is/was).
explain.memory: Pola “was/were supposed to” menyatakan rencana atau janji yang semestinya terlaksana, tetapi pada kenyataannya tidak terjadi.
explain.avoid: Selalu ucapin be + supposed to sebagai satu paket: is supposed to, was supposed to.

items.sentence: It's late. It's time we ___ home.

distractors.misconception: keeps a present-tense verb after 'it's high time', calquing 'sudah waktunya' plus a present verb
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “it's time + subjek”, kata kerjanya pakai lampau tak nyata, bukan bentuk sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: sesudah “it's high time” kata kerjanya dibiarin bentuk kini, kebawa pola “sudah waktunya” plus kata kerja biasa.

distractors.misconception: marks the clause after 'it's high time' with future 'will' because the action is still to come
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” nggak ngikut “it's time we”. Bentuk tetapnya past simple.
distractors.misconceptionId: “will” ditambahin sesudah “it's high time” karena aksinya memang belum terjadi.

distractors.misconception: uses the present progressive after 'it's high time' as if the action were already under way
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing ngegambarin yang lagi terjadi. “It's time” bilang yang seharusnya terjadi.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sedang-berlangsung dipakai sesudah “it's high time”, seolah aksinya udah jalan.

explain.why: “It's time we” diikuti lampau tak nyata walau maknanya sekarang: it's time we went home.
explain.rule: It's (high) time + subjek + past simple = sesuatu harusnya terjadi sekarang atau udah seharusnya terjadi.
explain.memory: It's time we went.
explain.avoid: Lihat “it's time” dengan subjek sesudahnya? Taruh kata kerjanya di past simple.

items.sentence: He talks about the city as if he ___ there, but he has never left our village.

distractors.misconception: keeps the real-possibility present after 'as if' although the sentence denies the comparison
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk sekarang ngesankan itu mungkin benar, padahal “he has never left our village” nunjukin nggak.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk kini nyata dipertahanin sesudah “as if”, padahal kalimatnya sendiri nyangkal perbandingannya.

distractors.misconception: reads 'as if' as reporting genuine experience with the present perfect
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect laporin pengalaman nyata. Dia nggak punya pengalaman itu.
distractors.misconceptionId: “as if” dibaca kayak laporan pengalaman nyata, jadi dipasangin present perfect.

distractors.misconception: puts conditional 'would' inside the 'as if' clause as if it were a result clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” tempatnya di klausa akibat, bukan di dalam klausa “as if”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” diselipin ke dalam klausa “as if”, ketukar sama klausa hasil pengandaian.

explain.why: Dia nggak pernah tinggal di sana, jadi perbandingan nggak nyatanya pakai past simple: as if he lived there.
explain.rule: As if / as though + past simple = nggak nyata sekarang. + bentuk sekarang = mungkin benar.
explain.memory: As if he lived there (padahal nggak).
explain.avoid: Perbandingannya jelas salah? Geser kata kerjanya satu langkah ke belakang.

items.sentence: If she had caught the earlier bus, she ___ here with us now.

distractors.misconception: places the result in the unreal past instead of the present
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have been” ngegambarin akibat lampau, padahal “now” naruh akibatnya di sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: akibatnya ditaruh di masa lalu yang nggak nyata, bukan di masa kini.

distractors.misconception: uses a past form without the modal required in the result clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “was” polos nyatain fakta nyata, padahal situasinya khayalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple polos “weren't” dipakai di induk kalimat akibat tanpa modal pengandai.

distractors.misconception: repeats past perfect in the main clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “had been” bentuk klausa if. Klausa akibat butuh “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: past perfect diulang lagi di induk kalimat.

explain.why: Ketinggalan bus itu lampau, tapi “now” bikin akibatnya sekarang, jadi pakai “would be”.
explain.rule: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (sebab lampau), would + kata kerja dasar (akibat sekarang).
explain.memory: Sebab lampau, akibat “now” → would be.
explain.avoid: Cari “now” atau “today” di akibatnya: itu berarti would + kata kerja dasar, bukan would have.

items.sentence: ___ the warning earlier, we would have cancelled the trip.

distractors.misconception: mixing formal inversion with the conjunction 'if' at the same time
distractors.whyFailsId: bener di gaya netral, tapi bentuk sasarannya buang “if” dan balik “had”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembalikan formal dan kata sambung “if” dipakai bersamaan.

distractors.misconception: using normal subject-verb order, missing the inversion signal
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “if” atau inversi, ini cuma kalimat berita, bukan pengandaian.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan subjek dan kata kerja tetap biasa jadi tanda pembalikannya hilang.

distractors.misconception: using the result-clause auxiliary structure at the start of the if-clause
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma “had” yang pindah ke depan. Subjeknya tetap sebelum participle.
distractors.misconceptionId: susunan kata bantu milik anak kalimat hasil ditaruh di awal anak kalimat syarat.

explain.why: Di gaya formal “if” hilang dan “had” pindah ke depan subjek: Had we received the warning.
explain.rule: Inversi formal: Had + subjek + past participle, … would have + past participle.
explain.memory: If we had → Had we.
explain.avoid: Hapus “if”, lalu tuker posisi subjek sama “had”; yang lain nggak pindah.

items.sentence: Rarely ___ such a quiet morning in this city.

distractors.misconception: Fronts the negative adverbial without applying the required subject-auxiliary inversion.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “Rarely” di depan, kata bantunya harus sebelum subjek.
distractors.misconceptionId: keterangan negatifnya dimajuin, tapi kata bantu “have” yang udah ada dibiarin di belakang subjek.

distractors.misconception: Fronts 'Never' with no auxiliary at all, ignoring both the inversion rule and the need for 'have' with 'before'.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada inversi dan nggak ada kata bantu. Kata keterangan di depan nuntut keduanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “Never” dimajuin tanpa kata bantu sama sekali, aturan pembalikan dan kebutuhan “have” sama-sama diabaikan.

distractors.misconception: Places 'never' after the auxiliary instead of at the very front of the sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: inversi pakai kata bantu (have/do/did), bukan kata kerja utama sendirian.
distractors.misconceptionId: “never” ditaruh sesudah kata bantunya, bukan di posisi paling depan kalimat.

explain.why: “Rarely” di depan memicu inversi: kata bantu “have” pindah ke depan “I”.
explain.rule: Kata keterangan negatif di depan (never, rarely, seldom, not only) + kata bantu + subjek + kata kerja.
explain.memory: Rarely have I…
explain.avoid: Rarely/never di depan? Susun kayak pertanyaan: have I seen.

items.sentence: Only when the storm passed ___ the harbour.

distractors.misconception: keeps ordinary statement order after a fronted restrictive phrase
distractors.whyFailsId: klausa “Only when” di depan maksa inversi di klausa utama.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan pernyataan biasa dipertahanin sesudah frasa pembatas dimajuin.

distractors.misconception: inverts the lexical verb directly
distractors.whyFailsId: inversi butuh kata bantu. Kata kerja utama sendirian nggak bisa pindah ke depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja utamanya langsung dibalik.

distractors.misconception: adds emphatic do but does not invert it with the subject
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” ada tapi tetap sesudah subjek, jadi nggak ada inversi.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu penegas ditambahin tapi nggak dibalik sama subjeknya.

explain.why: “Only when…” di depan memicu inversi kata bantu: did the boats leave.
explain.rule: Only + frasa waktu/syarat di depan → kata bantu + subjek + kata kerja dasar di klausa utama.
explain.memory: Only when … did the boats leave.
explain.avoid: Kalimatnya mulai dari “Only after/when/then”? Taruh did/does/have sebelum subjek.

items.sentence: The doctor insisted that the patient ___ in bed for a week.

distractors.misconception: softening the demand with a conditional 'would', as if the clause reported a hypothetical
distractors.whyFailsId: subjunctive nggak pakai -s, walau sesudah “the patient”.
distractors.misconceptionId: tuntutan dilembutin pakai “would”.

distractors.misconception: backshifting the verb as ordinary reported speech instead of keeping the base subjunctive
distractors.whyFailsId: “insisted” yang lampau nggak mundurin subjunctive-nya. Tetap polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dimundurin kayak laporan netral.

distractors.misconception: applying ordinary subject-verb agreement with a singular subject inside the demand clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” ngubah tuntutan jadi perkiraan. Tuntutan pakai kata kerja polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesesuaian subjek biasa dipaksain di klausa tuntutan.

explain.why: “Insisted that” ngenalin tuntutan, jadi kata kerjanya subjunctive polos: the patient stay.
explain.rule: Demand/insist/recommend/suggest + that + subjek + kata kerja dasar (tanpa -s, tanpa penanda waktu).
explain.memory: Insisted that she stay.
explain.avoid: Sesudah kata kerja tuntutan + that, tulis kata kerjanya persis kayak di kamus.

items.sentence: ___ the offer, she would move to Tokyo next spring.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'was' instead of the subjunctive 'were' required in formal hypothetical inversion.
distractors.whyFailsId: pengandaian terbalik selalu pakai “were”, nggak pernah “was”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “was” dipakai gantiin “were” yang diwajibin di pembalikan pengandaian formal.

distractors.misconception: Adds 'if' to a structure that already signals conditionality through inversion.
distractors.whyFailsId: “if” dan inversi nggak bisa muncul bareng. Pilih satu.
distractors.misconceptionId: “if” ditambahin ke susunan yang udah nandain pengandaian lewat pembalikan.

distractors.misconception: Drops the inversion, leaving a non-inverted fragment without 'if'.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa inversi atau “if”, ini bukan klausa pengandaian.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembalikannya dihilangin jadi tersisa penggalan tanpa “if”.

explain.why: Buang “if” dan pindahin “were” ke depan jadi pengandaian formal: Were she to accept the offer.
explain.rule: Pengandaian formal kecil kemungkinan: Were + subjek + to + kata kerja dasar, … would + kata kerja dasar.
explain.memory: If she were to → Were she to.
explain.avoid: Tulis “If she were to accept”, lalu hapus “if” dan tuker: Were she to accept.

items.sentence: Ms. Rina is our teacher. We like ___ very much.

distractors.misconception: subject-pronoun-in-object-position
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk subjek, padahal sesudah “like” butuh bentuk objek.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti subjek ditaruh di posisi objek.

distractors.misconception: possessive-form-as-person-object
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya “punya dia”, bukan orangnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk pemilik dipakai untuk menggantikan orangnya.

distractors.misconception: pronoun gender does not match the person
distractors.whyFailsId: untuk laki-laki, padahal “Ms. Rina” perempuan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti untuk laki-laki dan perempuan tertukar.

explain.why: Titik-titiknya ada sesudah kata kerja “like” dan menunjuk “Ms. Rina”. Bentuk objeknya “her”.
explain.rule: Subjek: “I”, “he”, “she”. Sesudah kata kerja: “me”, “him”, “her”. Sebelum kata benda: “my”, “his”, “her”. Berdiri sendiri: “mine”, “his”, “hers”.
explain.memory: Sesudah kata kerja: “me”, “him”, “her”, “us”, “them”.
explain.avoid: Cek dulu posisi titik-titiknya: sebelum kata kerja, sesudah kata kerja, atau sebelum kata benda.

distractors.misconceptionId: “my” dipakai tanpa kata benda sesudahnya.

distractors.misconception: object-pronoun-substitution

distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk objek dipakai untuk menyebut pemilik.

distractors.misconception: subject pronoun used to show ownership

distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti subjek dipakai untuk menunjukkan pemilik.

explain.why: Nggak ada kata benda sesudah titik-titik, jadi kata pemiliknya harus berdiri sendiri, yaitu “mine”.
explain.rule: Subjek: “I”, “he”, “she”. Sesudah kata kerja: “me”, “him”, “her”. Sebelum kata benda: “my”, “his”, “her”. Berdiri sendiri: “mine”, “his”, “hers”.
explain.memory: “My bag”, tapi “the bag is mine”.
explain.avoid: Cek dulu posisi titik-titiknya: sebelum kata kerja, sesudah kata kerja, atau sebelum kata benda.

distractors.misconceptionId: “be” dicocokkan dengan kata terdekat, bukan dengan seluruh subjek.

distractors.misconception: singular be
distractors.whyFailsId: untuk satu orang, padahal di sini ada dua orang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk tunggal “is” dipakai untuk dua orang.

distractors.misconception: base form
